description: Within the substantive result, place the file-change array first, existing selected-mode result requirements second, and derived task-summary array third. Preserve the tool audit and universal suffix outside this substantive result.

definitions.file_change: One observed changed file, with metadata and all recorded edit locations.
definitions.subtask: A named task association stored in the file-change record; not a retrospective authorization.
definitions.edit_ids: Exact edit references associated with that subtask in this file.
definitions.task_summary: A derived grouping of file edits by recorded subtask ID; its task text is copied from the source record.
definitions.source_ref: Actual source-record or invocation reference; null when not available. EXAMPLE references are never runtime evidence.

instructions: Build file_changes from observed file differences in the declared comparison scope.
For each changed file, report both metadata snapshots and every edit's before and after location and value.
Use subtasks:[] when no task association is recorded; do not invent a task association to justify an extra edit.
Subtask associations name edit_ids within the same file-change record; references must resolve.
Build task_summary only after file_changes. Group by subtask_id and copy the subtask text.
For each summary entry, list all associated file edits with file-change ID, edit ID, old/new paths, kind, and old/new locations.
An edit associated with multiple subtasks appears once under each relevant subtask.
Keep file_changes as the authoritative evidence; task_summary is a derived index.
Null denotes unavailable metadata or source reference; an observed absence must be preserved in the actual lookup record, not inferred from null.
A file-change report cannot establish completion of non-file tasks or tasks that yielded no change.
Do not alter current preplan requirements or activate this draft in the governing AGENTS.md.
File changes without subtask association remain in the first array with subtasks:[]; no association is invented for the task summary.
The substantive result has three ordered items: file-change array, the selected mode's existing result object, and task-summary array.
Keep every existing required result field in the middle object; retain optional fields when applicable.
Keep the verbatim-tool-invocation audit and universal profile/status suffix in their existing second and third outer-report positions.
Do not put the entire original report inside the middle object.
cross_record_rules: file_change_id values are unique within the report.
edit_id values are unique within their file-change record.
Every subtask edit_id resolves to an edit in that record.
The same subtask_id has the same subtask text wherever it appears.
The summary is the exact grouping of associated edits, with no invented or omitted entries.

validation.example_schema_check: Illustrative report checked for required keys, closed objects, value types, enumerations, and scalar bounds.
validation.derivation_check: Task-summary entries derive from the first substantive array. Existing mode result fields occupy only the middle substantive item; audit and suffix retain their original outer positions.
validation.limits: Cross-record invariants and live provenance require additional verification in actual use; no Chat-mode effectiveness test performed.
